claims.text: A homogeneous solid-solution microstructure that minimizes copper segregation enables formation of a continuous, adherent passive oxide film.
The passive oxide film enhances corrosion resistance.
The passive oxide film maintains mechanical strength.
The passive oxide film provides high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Low copper content produces a single-phase, homogeneous solid solution in the proposed lightweight alloy.
The passivating scale is primarily composed of light-element oxides such as Al2O3 and TiO2.
The passivating oxide scale forms uniformly on a homogeneous alloy surface.
Uniform elemental distribution prevents heavy-element clusters from disrupting oxide-barrier continuity.
Avoiding copper segregation reduces corrosion current density.
Avoiding copper segregation resists oxidation-induced degradation.
Avoiding copper segregation preserves mechanical integrity.
Variants with minimized copper segregation will have lower corrosion current densities than variants with higher copper content or induced segregation.
Variants with minimized copper segregation will form more coherent oxide scales at high temperature.
Variants with minimized copper segregation will have superior mechanical properties.
Copper segregation produces discontinuous oxide scales that compromise mechanical strength.
Excessive copper content can induce detrimental elemental segregation.
Thermal treatments can induce enough segregation to defeat the proposed protection mechanism.
Temperatures or oxidizing potentials beyond the protective oxide's stability window will cause the mechanism to fail.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome describes the baseline as having higher copper content or induced segregation, whereas the baseline field defines it as having optimally low, uniformly distributed copper. This makes the direction of the controlled comparison ambiguous.
